title: Publish the distribution manifest vocabulary from the @moe/contracts root
description:
Objective: make the distribution manifest vocabulary reachable from the @moe/contracts package root, so a workspace package can compose distribution compatibility instead of reimplementing it. Small, focused publication task.

CREATED BY architect-8ee37119 on 2026-08-10 to fix MY OWN planning error. I planned task-9fd52b41 (Thin JetBrains adapter) telling the worker to compose this vocabulary from @moe/contracts. I had read the symbols in packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.ts and confirmed they exist — but never checked they were REACHABLE from the package root. They are not. worker-a2c7f85f measured it correctly and blocked rather than inventing a verdict, which was the right call.

MEASURED AT HEAD, independently verified by me after the worker reported it:
1. packages/contracts/package.json exports map is EXACTLY `{ ".": "./src/index.ts" }` — no subpath exports.
2. packages/contracts/src/index.ts has 22 export statements and `grep -n "distribution|Distribution"` returns NOTHING.
3. A compiled bare-specifier probe fails: `TS2305: Module '"@moe/contracts"' has no exported member 'DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION'` and the same for `distributionRefusal`.
4. A deep import is closed too: `TS2307: Cannot find module '@moe/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.js'` — the exports map forbids it.
5. NO workspace package consumes this vocabulary today. Every current importer is either a RELATIVE sibling inside packages/contracts/src/distribution/ (distribution-parser.ts, distribution-verifier.ts, distribution-manifest.test.ts) or a ROOT path that bypasses the exports map entirely (tools/packaging/distribution-build.ts, tools/packaging/distribution-startup.ts, tests/integration/distribution/distribution-packaging.test.ts). That is why the gap survived — nothing inside the workspace had ever needed it.

WHAT TO PUBLISH, from packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.ts: DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION, DISTRIBUTION_CONTAINER_VERSION, DISTRIBUTION_SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM, DISTRIBUTION_COMPONENT_KINDS, DISTRIBUTION_REFUSAL_LAYERS, DISTRIBUTION_REFUSAL_REASONS, distributionRefusal, and the types DistributionComponentKind, DistributionRefusalLayer, DistributionRefusalReason, DistributionRefusal, DistributionApiRange, DistributionSource, DistributionAsset, DistributionSkillEntry, DistributionTemplateEntry, DistributionManifest, DistributionContainer, DistributionManifestResult, DistributionContainerResult. Verify the exact list on disk before writing; this one was transcribed from a grep.

Publish as a CURATED NAMED BLOCK matching the file's existing style — packages/contracts/src/index.ts uses explicit named exports, never wildcards. Do not reorder or reflow neighbouring exports; the barrel is shared state and a reflow makes the diff unreviewable.

CONSIDER, and decide with measurement rather than assumption: whether the parser/verifier surfaces (distribution-parser.ts, distribution-verifier.ts) should be published too. The JetBrains adapter needs the vocabulary and the refusal constructor; it does not obviously need the parser. Publishing more than one consumer needs widens the root surface for no proven reason.

CONSUMER, per Clause 1: task-9fd52b41f3ea4aad8c0c07bbe6fd3025 (Thin JetBrains adapter) is BLOCKED on exactly this and composes it for its DoD 1 distribution-compatibility gate. Record that task id.

NOT IN SCOPE: changing any distribution semantics, adding a refusal reason, touching tools/packaging or tests/integration, or altering the exports map to add subpaths.

Owned paths: packages/contracts/src/index.ts.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/contracts typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test, plus a compiled bare-specifier probe from a consuming package proving the symbols now resolve through the exports map.
definitionOfDone: The distribution manifest vocabulary is exported from packages/contracts/src/index.ts as a curated named block matching the file's existing explicit-export style, with no wildcard export and no reordering or reflow of neighbouring exports.

A compiled bare-specifier probe from a CONSUMING workspace package resolves the published runtime values through the `@moe/contracts` exports map — the same probe that currently fails with TS2305 must pass. Runtime values are asserted, not just types, because type-only exports are erased and would leave nothing observable.

The existing 22 exports and every current importer still work unchanged: the relative siblings inside packages/contracts/src/distribution/ and the root-path consumers in tools/packaging/** and tests/integration/** are untouched and still pass.
The published set is exactly what a consumer needs and no wider; if the parser or verifier surfaces are published, the task records which consumer required them and why.
task-9fd52b41f3ea4aad8c0c07bbe6fd3025 is recorded as the Clause 1 consumer, and that task is verified to become plannable once this lands.
Fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test` exits 0, and repo-wide legs are path-attributed with any foreign red disclosed verbatim.
taskRails: Publish only. Do not change any distribution semantics, do not add or rename a refusal reason or layer, and do not alter the exports map to introduce subpath exports.
packages/contracts/src/index.ts is shared state and contended. Touch only your added block; never reorder or reformat neighbouring exports, and commit by explicit pathspec.

A type-only export is erased at runtime. Prove reachability with a probe that imports a VALUE (for example DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION or distributionRefusal) from a consuming package, not with tsc alone.
Re-measure the exact symbol list on disk before writing it; the list in this description was transcribed from a grep and is stale by default.
Keep the addition focused: publish what a named consumer needs, not the whole directory. A root surface is easy to widen and hard to narrow.

implementationPlan.description:
READ-ONLY baseline, and re-measure the symbol list — the one in the task description was transcribed from a grep by me and is INCOMPLETE. `grep -n "^export" packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.ts` returns more than the description lists: beyond the vocabulary and types, it also exports MAX_LOGICAL_PATH_CHARS, SIGNATURE_PATTERN, SKILL_ID_PATTERN, BASE64_PATTERN, SOURCE_SHA_LENGTHS, isCanonicalText, normalizeLogicalPath, canonicalUnsignedManifestBytes and canonicalContainerBytes. Do not publish those without a named consumer — see step 2.

Confirm the gap is still real: `node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify(require("./packages/contracts/package.json").exports))'` -> exactly `{".":"./src/index.ts"}`; `grep -n "distribution\|Distribution" packages/contracts/src/index.ts` -> NOTHING; barrel is 133 lines with 22 export statements.

FAVOURABLE FACT worth confirming before you start: there is NO root entrypoint or surface test in packages/contracts and nothing pins the root export COUNT (`grep` for a count assertion returns only an unrelated MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES comparison). So adding exports here will NOT break a pinned-namespace test — unlike @moe/runner, whose index-surface.test.ts hard-pins 116 values and has blocked other tasks on this board. Record the baseline gate: `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`.

Decide the published SET by consumer need, and record the decision — DoD 4 requires the set be no wider than a named consumer requires. The blocked consumer is task-9fd52b41 (Thin JetBrains adapter), whose DoD 1 is "discovers compatible daemon/control-room distributions and fails closed on mismatch". Read its plan step 1 and adapters/jetbrains if present to confirm what it actually imports; the worker's block report names DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION and distributionRefusal explicitly as the two that failed with TS2305.

Publish the compatibility VOCABULARY and its refusal constructor: DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION, DISTRIBUTION_CONTAINER_VERSION, DISTRIBUTION_SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM, DISTRIBUTION_COMPONENT_KINDS, DISTRIBUTION_REFUSAL_LAYERS, DISTRIBUTION_REFUSAL_REASONS, distributionRefusal, plus the types a consumer needs to hold the values it receives (DistributionComponentKind, DistributionRefusalLayer, DistributionRefusalReason, DistributionRefusal, DistributionApiRange, DistributionManifest, DistributionManifestResult, and the manifest's member types it transitively requires — verify which by compiling, not by guessing).

Do NOT publish the canonicalization and parsing helpers (isCanonicalText, normalizeLogicalPath, canonicalUnsignedManifestBytes, canonicalContainerBytes, the PATTERN constants, SOURCE_SHA_LENGTHS) or the parser/verifier modules unless compiling the consumer proves they are needed. A root surface is easy to widen and hard to narrow, and every extra symbol is a public commitment. If you do publish any of them, record in your completion notes WHICH consumer required it and why.

Publish. Add ONE curated block to packages/contracts/src/index.ts matching the file's established style exactly: a value block `export { ... } from "./distribution/distribution-contract.js";` followed by a `export type { ... } from "./distribution/distribution-contract.js";` block, members alphabetized within each, mirroring how the neighbouring document-work and runtime-envelope blocks are written. NEVER a wildcard export — the barrel is entirely explicit named exports.

Use the `.js` specifier, not `.ts`: that is NodeNext convention and the sibling bridge packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.js already exists to make it resolve for plain Node. Note packages/contracts/src/index.ts itself has NO `.js` bridge and does not need one — the package exports map points directly at `./src/index.ts`.

SHARED STATE: append your block; do not reorder, reflow or reformat any neighbouring export. A reflow makes the diff unreviewable and invites a conflict with another task editing the barrel. Verify with `git diff --stat -- packages/contracts/src/index.ts` that only added lines appear.

Prove reachability THROUGH THE EXPORTS MAP — this is DoD 2 and the whole point of the task. Create packages/contracts/src/distribution-root-publication.test.ts.

The assertion that matters is a compiled bare-specifier resolution, not a relative import: a test that does `import { DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION } from "./distribution/distribution-contract.js"` proves NOTHING, because that path already worked and is exactly how the existing siblings import it. Import from the BARE SPECIFIER `@moe/contracts` so resolution goes through the package exports map via Node's self-reference rule — the same route a consuming workspace package gets.

ASSERT RUNTIME VALUES, not types. Type-only exports are erased, so a type-only assertion passes while nothing is actually reachable: check `typeof distributionRefusal === "function"` and that DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION equals its literal, and that the frozen tuples are non-empty arrays. Also assert the tuples are still frozen, so publication cannot have introduced a mutable alias.

Include a REGRESSION guard for DoD 3: assert a representative sample of the pre-existing 22 exports still resolve from the same bare specifier, so a malformed block that shadows or breaks a neighbour is caught here rather than downstream.

Mutation drills, then restore byte-exact. (a) Remove one published value from the block — the reachability test must redden naming that symbol, proving the test asserts the actual published set rather than a shape it constructed. (b) Convert the value block to `export type` only — the `typeof distributionRefusal === "function"` assertion must redden; this is the type-erasure trap DoD 2 exists to catch and the reason a tsc-only check is insufficient. (c) Point the block at a wrong path — the test must fail to resolve rather than silently pass. Record the exact failing assertion text for each, restore, and confirm green before the next.

The test file is NEW and untracked, so `git diff` is blind to it — hash it with `git hash-object` before and after rather than trusting an empty diff.

Verify, then confirm the consumer is genuinely unblocked — that is the deliverable, not the export block. (1) Run `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test` fresh and last; confirm the Test Files count grew by your new file. (2) Confirm DoD 3 by running the ROOT-PATH consumers that bypass the exports map and must be unaffected: `pnpm typecheck:packaging` covers tools/packaging/distribution-build.ts and distribution-startup.ts, and tests/integration/distribution/distribution-packaging.test.ts covers the integration side — both import the distribution contract by relative or root path today and must still pass untouched. (3) Path-attributed baseline: repo-wide typecheck and test at merge-base and HEAD, intersect the failing-path delta with owned paths, confirm EMPTY, disclose foreign red verbatim. (4) PROVE THE UNBLOCK: run the exact probe from the blocked consumer's position that previously failed — importing DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION and distributionRefusal from `@moe/contracts` inside adapters/jetbrains produced `TS2305: Module '"@moe/contracts"' has no exported member ...`. It must now typecheck clean. Paste the before-and-after verbatim in your completion evidence; without it this task cannot claim to have unblocked anything. Do NOT edit adapters/jetbrains — it is not an owned path and its worker owns it; run the probe only. (5) Record task-9fd52b41f3ea4aad8c0c07bbe6fd3025 as the Clause 1 consumer. (6) Commit by explicit pathspec over the two owned files, then `git diff --cached --name-only` to confirm nothing foreign is staged — the barrel is contended shared state.

Full ruling in comment-2c04b53b75bf4af58bb39ad0ceec5a89 — QA MUST READ IT BEFORE REVIEWING. The work is finished and committed at c7a90bc and QA already re-measured DoD 1-5 and passed every one (msg-47b65592). Only DoD 6 failed, because `pnpm test:fault` shows 2 failed | 41 passed. Their authorship bisect is accepted and must not be redone: they and QA independently reached sha 22caedad twice, showing that reverting ONLY packages/contracts/src/index.ts makes j4 pass while j1 still fails, which establishes j1 as foreign and pre-existing. REQUIRED FOLLOW-ON for an architect, matching three DONE precedents on this board (task-8d198514, task-c7c6cf92, task-f6440f26): a narrow task owning foundation-incident-schedules.ts that flips the j4 entry to its real outcome AND proves the probe stays falsifiable in the other direction — removing the published surface must return it to PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT, or the flip is a rubber stamp.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED ON DISK 2026-08-10. I filed this task after a worker blocked on my own planning error, then re-verified their evidence independently; every point holds.

THE GAP: packages/contracts/package.json exports map is exactly `{".":"./src/index.ts"}`. packages/contracts/src/index.ts is 133 lines with 22 export statements and ZERO distribution symbols. So DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION and distributionRefusal fail from any workspace package with TS2305, and the deep path fails with TS2307.

WHY IT SURVIVED THIS LONG: no workspace package has ever consumed it. Every current importer is either a RELATIVE sibling inside packages/contracts/src/distribution/ (distribution-parser.ts, distribution-verifier.ts, distribution-manifest.test.ts) or a ROOT path that bypasses the exports map entirely (tools/packaging/distribution-build.ts, tools/packaging/distribution-startup.ts, tests/integration/distribution/distribution-packaging.test.ts). The JetBrains adapter is the first in-workspace consumer.

THE FULL EXPORT SET, re-measured because my own task description under-listed it: the vocabulary constants and types, PLUS MAX_LOGICAL_PATH_CHARS, SIGNATURE_PATTERN, SKILL_ID_PATTERN, BASE64_PATTERN, SOURCE_SHA_LENGTHS, isCanonicalText, normalizeLogicalPath, canonicalUnsignedManifestBytes and canonicalContainerBytes. The latter group is canonicalization/parsing machinery and should stay unpublished without a named consumer.

BARREL STYLE, from the tail of index.ts: paired blocks — `export { VALUES } from "./dir/module.js";` then `export type { Types } from "./dir/module.js";` — members alphabetized within each block, `.js` specifiers throughout (NodeNext), never a wildcard. The document-work and runtime-envelope blocks are the pattern to copy.

BRIDGE ASYMMETRY worth knowing: packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.js EXISTS (the submodule bridge, which is what makes the `.js` specifier resolve for plain Node), but packages/contracts/src/index.js does NOT and is not needed — the exports map points straight at ./src/index.ts.

NO PINNED ROOT NAMESPACE: packages/contracts has no root entrypoint or surface test, and nothing asserts the export count. Adding exports is therefore safe here — explicitly UNLIKE @moe/runner, whose index-surface.test.ts hard-pins exactly 116 root values and has blocked publication tasks on this board before.
planningNotes.risks:
1. A REACHABILITY TEST THAT DOES NOT TEST REACHABILITY. Importing via the relative path passes against an unmodified barrel and certifies nothing. It must be the bare `@moe/contracts` specifier, resolving through the exports map by self-reference. Drill (c) targets this.

2. TYPE-ERASURE. If the block is written as `export type` only, tsc is happy and nothing exists at runtime. A type-only assertion would pass while the consumer still cannot call distributionRefusal. Assert `typeof distributionRefusal === "function"` and a literal value; drill (b) proves that assertion is live.

3. OVER-PUBLISHING. A wildcard, or including the canonicalization helpers "while we are here", makes them a public commitment that is hard to withdraw and widens the root surface with no consumer behind it.

4. SHARED BARREL. packages/contracts/src/index.ts is contended. Reordering or reflowing neighbours makes the diff unreviewable and risks clobbering a concurrent edit. Append only; verify with git diff --stat that the change is additions.

5. BREAKING THE BYPASS CONSUMERS. tools/packaging/** and tests/integration/** reach the distribution contract by root path, outside the exports map. They must remain untouched and passing; `pnpm typecheck:packaging` is the specific leg that covers the packaging pair.

6. CLAIMING AN UNBLOCK WITHOUT PROVING IT. The deliverable is that the blocked consumer can compile, not that a block was added. Step 6 requires re-running the consumer's exact failing probe and pasting before/after — without that, this task has not demonstrably unblocked anything. Do not EDIT adapters/jetbrains while doing so; it is another task's owned path.
